record.what_it_does: Open-source CRM with a custom data model, REST/GraphQL APIs, webhooks and MCP.
record.auth_notes: API keys are created in Settings → Developers → API, are shown once, and are sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <key>'. OAuth 2.0 uses the authorization code flow, with PKCE recommended (S256). Client credentials give server-to-server tokens with workspace-level access. Clients register dynamically through RFC 7591 at POST /oauth/register, with no dashboard setup. Discovery is at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server; the other endpoints are /oauth/authorize and /oauth/token. Scopes are 'api' (full read/write on the Core and Metadata APIs; the default) and 'profile'. The base URL is https://api.twenty.com for Cloud and the instance domain for self-hosted. The MCP endpoint accepts OAuth 2.1 or an API key.
record.access_notes: Cloud has no permanent free plan. It offers a 30-day trial with no credit card, then Pro ($9/user/month), Organization ($39/user/month) or Enterprise (from $50k/year). Cloud Pro and Organization are billed yearly. All paid plans include the REST & GraphQL API, webhooks and the MCP server. Cloud API limits are 50/min on Pro, 100/min on Organization and custom on Enterprise. Self-hosting the open-source core is free and includes the full API. OAuth clients self-register dynamically; the docs describe no vendor app review, only the end user's consent screen.
record.api_breadth_notes: REST and GraphQL are generated from each workspace's schema. They give CRUD, batch and (in GraphQL) upsert on every standard object (people, companies, opportunities, tasks, notes, attachments and others) and on custom objects. Batches can hold up to 60 records per request. A Metadata API (/rest/metadata/, /metadata/) creates and changes objects, fields and relations. Across all objects this comes to well over 50 operations.
record.mcp_notes: https://{your-workspace-url}/mcp, streamable-http, OAuth 2.1 or an API-key Bearer token. The URL is per workspace, so cloud and self-hosted instances each have their own. Community servers also exist (e.g. jezweb/twenty-mcp).
record.blocker_notes: Minor caveats. The base URL varies by workspace and deployment (api.twenty.com vs a self-hosted domain). The OpenAPI spec is generated per workspace at /rest/open-api/core and /rest/open-api/metadata rather than published statically. Cloud rate limits are low (50/min on Pro). Cloud needs a paid plan after the 30-day trial. A free self-hosted instance works for development. Webhooks are configured in the Settings UI and have no event filtering.

evidence.quote: Read and write records over REST and GraphQL, get webhooks when records change, and connect apps with OAuth.
No manual setup needed — register programmatically.
Self-hosting the open source core is free.
Both REST and GraphQL support batching up to 60 records per request.
Validate signatures to ensure requests are authentic.
(transport: streamable-http; auth: OAuth 2.1 or an API-key Bearer token)
